offlineReview.classification: repeated single log-row interpretation, not distinct source rows
offlineReview.observation: The dominant thinking line appears 79 times; its underlying original log row occurs once. The attempt reached the output cap with no accepted tool call or visible answer.
A single statement choosing the same test command repeats 398 times; no tool call or visible answer was accepted before the output cap.
Each of three punctuation-analysis statements occurs 120 times. Earlier fenced code is excluded; the trigger is outside it. No tool call or visible answer was accepted before the output cap.

limitations: Small exposed development sample on one machine, model and runtime; no qualified false-positive rate or generalization estimate.
Successful task completion is not proof every intermediate generation was useful; any trigger requires generation-level review.
The detector observes thinking only. Tool arguments, visible prose, incoming tool/test output and summary generations are outside its proposed scope.
Coalesced durable event chunks recover complete-line content but not exact provider token timing; trigger times are recorded event boundaries.
No controlled interruptions/retries were run. Offline crossings establish neither runtime savings nor task recovery outcomes.
No held-out tasks or checkers were inspected, and no threshold tuning or production activation was performed.
conclusion: Further controlled work is justified, without default activation: all three triggers align with observed repetitive generations that later hit the output cap without accepted tool calls or visible answers, while none of 101 normally terminated generations trigger. This small exposed sample establishes no qualified false-positive rate and does not demonstrate that an earlier interruption would preserve recovery or save runtime.
